# Design leader election using Redis leases

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/design-leader-election-using-redis-leases)** — free, no card: the interview workspace, an AI interviewer to push back on your design, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You are given $$N$$ stateless service instances, each executing the same code. At any moment, at most one of them may act as leader and perform a singleton responsibility — such as driving a scheduler, serving as the only writer to a partition, or consuming from a queue. The remaining instances are followers waiting to take over if needed.

Design a lease-based leader-election protocol using Redis for coordination. You may assume one primary Redis endpoint for this exercise. Any Redis feature is allowed, including `SET NX PX`, Lua scripts, and Pub/Sub.

Your design must cover:

- How a leader is elected so that two leaders never exist simultaneously.
- How failover works when the current leader crashes or becomes unhealthy; a replacement must be promoted within a bounded time.
- How leadership remains time-limited through a lease or heartbeat mechanism that the active leader continuously renews while healthy.
- Correctness concerns: split brain, a crashed leader incorrectly remaining leader, clock-skew assumptions, network interruptions, and GC / stop-the-world pauses.
- Operational concerns: what metrics and logs you would add, and what the system should do when Redis is unreachable.

Submit a precise protocol description, the Redis data model including keys, stored values, and TTLs, and the behavior for relevant edge cases.

Constraints and assumptions:

- $$N$$ stateless instances, on the order of tens such as $$N \le 50$$; every instance runs the same election loop.
- One primary Redis endpoint is available. Redis is not a CP consensus system — be explicit about where that bounds the safety guarantee.
- Coordination traffic is very small: only a few keys and a low rate of acquire/renew operations. Throughput is not the main concern; failover latency and safety are.
- Network partitions, packet loss, and process pauses such as GC or stop-the-world events are all in scope.
- A brief period with zero leaders is acceptable. Two leaders performing conflicting work is never acceptable. Safety dominates liveness.
- Do not assume synchronized wall clocks across instances.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

A lease is only safe if the leader can prove it still holds it, so think about expiry, renewal, and what happens when a leader pauses.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Reach for SET NX PX for acquisition, a Lua script for compare-and-renew or release, and Pub/Sub or polling for followers to detect vacancy.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Watch the split-brain window between lease expiry and a new leader taking over, and make the singleton work idempotent or fenced.

</details>
